CHAPTER 10

To Production
走向生产环境

Anything that can go wrong will go wrong.
——Murphy’s law

凡是可能出错的事，终将出错。
——墨菲定律

When you’re starting your career as a programmer, production can feel both intimidating and exciting. Production is where your code moves from development into a live environment used by real people. This is the culmination of all the planning, problem-solving, and late nights.

刚开启程序员职业生涯时，生产环境既令人生畏又令人兴奋。生产环境是你的代码从开发进入真实用户使用的线上环境的地方。这是所有规划、解决问题和熬夜的成果汇聚之处。

Production represents one of the final stages in the SDLC. It’s where your application will face its true test: serving real end users, handling real data, and operating under extensive workloads.

生产环境是软件开发生命周期（SDLC）的最后阶段之一。在这里，你的应用将面对真正的考验：服务真实的终端用户、处理真实的数据、在繁重的负载下运行。

You’re leaving the safety net of your local development environment where it’s just you and your code and entering a space where actual people are depending on your work. When issues arise, they are visible to everyone. You might think of your codebase as just another application, but in the hands of users, it becomes a tool that drives business value and creates meaningful change in the world.

你正在离开本地开发环境那张安全网——那里只有你和你的代码——进入一个真实的人依赖你工作的空间。问题一旦出现，人人都看得到。你也许觉得自己的代码库不过是又一个应用，但在用户手中，它成了驱动业务价值、在世界上创造真实改变的工具。

In this chapter, you’ll gain a better understanding and appreciation for production. You will begin to start thinking about building production-ready code earlier on in the SDLC. A key component of this is understanding the fundamental differences between development and production environments and how to bridge that gap effectively.

在本章中，你会对生产环境有更深的理解和体会。你会开始在 SDLC 更早的阶段就思考如何构建可上线的代码。其中一个关键组成部分，是理解开发环境与生产环境之间的根本差异，以及如何有效地弥合这一差距。

The Complexities of Production Environments

“Houston, we have a problem.” These famous words from the near-disastrous Apollo 13 mission remind us that things can go wrong even in controlled environments. While software development rarely involves life-or-death stakes, unexpected issues can arise when transitioning to different environments, especially production.

“休斯顿，我们出问题了。”阿波罗 13 号任务险些酿成灾难，这句名言提醒我们：即使在受控环境中也会出问题。虽然软件开发很少涉及生死攸关的利害关系，但在切换到不同环境、尤其是生产环境时，意想不到的问题可能冒出来。

Imagine you and your team have been working on a new product for months. You have sufficient test coverage, and your QA teams have put it through the wringer in various environments. You get sign-off from all teams involved, and you’re ready to go.

想象一下：你和团队已经为一个新产品忙活了好几个月。你有充分的测试覆盖率，QA 团队也已经在各种环境里把它折腾了个遍。所有相关团队都签了字，你准备就绪。

All the right buttons are pushed, and your project takes its maiden voyage to production. At first, everything seems fine as traffic starts flowing in. But suddenly, chaos erupts. Users report bugs, performance issues appear unexpectedly, and your monitoring system along with your inbox becomes flooded with alerts.

该按的按钮都按了，你的项目首次启航前往生产。起初，随着流量涌入，一切似乎正常。但突然间，混乱爆发了。用户报告 bug，性能问题凭空出现，你的监控系统连同邮箱被警报淹没。

What happened? The code worked on your machine. It worked in every environment you tested. If you’ve experienced this scenario, you’re not alone. It underscores why production matters so much. It’s not just the final stop for our code. It’s the real world, the ultimate test, where actual users interact with our applications.

发生了什么？代码在你机器上是好的，在你测试过的每个环境里也是好的。如果你经历过这种场景，你并不孤单。这正说明了为什么生产环境如此重要。它不只是代码的终点站，它是真实世界、是终极考验，真实用户在那里与我们的应用交互。

Although your software might work in test environments, its true value is determined in how it performs in production with real users. The differences between development and production often manifest in two ways: users interacting with your application in unpredictable ways, and the infamous “it works on my machine,” where code behaves differently across environments. Let’s explore both challenges and discover some practical strategies for bridging this gap.

尽管你的软件在测试环境里能跑，它的真正价值却取决于它在生产环境中面对真实用户时的表现。开发与生产之间的差异通常以两种方式显现：用户以不可预测的方式与你的应用交互；以及臭名昭著的“在我机器上是好的”——代码在不同环境中表现不一。让我们探究这两大挑战，并找出弥合差距的实用策略。

Users Are Unpredictable

Developers often fall into the trap of thinking that they can anticipate how their users will interact with their applications. Sometimes you may lack a complete picture of your user base. Sometimes you think you know more than you actually do. Both scenarios can lead to misaligned expectations between developers and users.

开发者常常掉进一个陷阱：以为自己能预料用户会怎么与应用交互。有时你对用户群缺乏完整的了解，有时你自以为懂得比实际多。这两种情况都会导致开发者与用户之间的期望错位。

While this is absolutely important to the success of a project, there is no number of tests that you can write or scenarios that you can simulate that can replicate the unpredictable nature of real-world usage. This is why users are your ultimate test.

尽管这对项目成功绝对重要，但无论你写多少测试、模拟多少场景，都无法复制真实世界使用中那种不可预测性。这就是为什么用户才是你终极的测试。

A “Users Are Unpredictable” Story
一则“用户不可预测”的故事

Dan here. One of my first jobs out of college was as a Level 2 support specialist. A user called me asking why the “drink holder” on his computer was malfunctioning. I replied, “Sir, computers don’t have drink holders.” It turned out he was referring to the CD-ROM drive. This incident perfectly illustrates how no amount of testing could have prepared us for a user mistaking a CD-ROM drive for a drink holder.
我是 Dan。我大学毕业后的第一份工作就是二级支持专员。一位用户打电话给我，问他电脑上的“杯架”为什么坏了。我回答说：“先生，电脑上没有杯架。”结果他指的是 CD-ROM 光驱。这件事完美地说明：无论多少测试，都无法让我们预料到有用户会把 CD-ROM 光驱当成杯架。

The following are factors that contribute to user unpredictability:

以下是导致用户不可预测性的因素：

  • Real-world data: Even the most meticulously designed test data can’t anticipate the creative ways users will interact with your forms. They’ll input data in ways that would seem plausible only in a Hollywood screenplay.真实世界的数据：即便是最精心设计的测试数据，也预料不到用户会以多有创意的方式与你的表单交互。他们输入数据的方式，只有在好莱坞剧本里才显得合理。
  • Scale and concurrency: Real-world traffic can expose scalability issues that weren’t apparent in controlled environments with test data.规模与并发：真实流量可能暴露在受控环境、用测试数据时并不明显的可扩展性问题。
  • Diverse environments: Real users have all sorts of environments. This includes varying operating systems, system resources, security settings, browser vendor and version, network latency, and more.多样化的环境：真实用户拥有各种各样的环境，包括不同的操作系统、系统资源、安全设置、浏览器厂商与版本、网络延迟等等。
  • Environmental drift: Different versions of software or libraries in different environments can cause inconsistent behavior that wasn’t present during testing.环境漂移：不同环境中软件或库的版本不同，可能导致测试时未曾出现的不一致行为。
  • Unexpected use cases: Users might interact with your software in ways developers didn’t anticipate, revealing edge cases or unforeseen scenarios.意料之外的用例：用户可能以开发者未曾预料的方式与你的软件交互，暴露出边缘情况或未曾预见的场景。

To prepare for the unknown of the real world, you can adopt practices like canary releases, A/B testing, and robust observability (comprehensive monitoring through logging, metrics, and distributed tracing). These methods leverage the power of real-world user testing while minimizing risk.

为了应对真实世界的未知，你可以采用金丝雀发布、A/B 测试和健壮的可观测性（通过日志、指标和分布式追踪进行全面监控）等做法。这些方法在最小化风险的同时，利用了真实用户测试的威力。

“But It Works on My Machine”

You get a notification for a new issue that was filed in production. You read through the description and realize this is a feature you worked on. You turn to your laptop to run through the scenario and see whether you can reproduce the issue and, of course, you can’t. Works on my machine, must be user error. “Unable to reproduce” is the phrase developers use to close issues in these situations.

你收到一条通知，生产环境提交了一个新问题。你读完描述，发现这是你做过的一个功能。你转向笔记本电脑复现场景，看看能否重现这个问题——当然，你重现不出来。在我机器上是好的，那一定是用户的错。“无法重现”就是开发者在这种情况下关掉问题单时用的说法。

原书第 241 页

In software development, “works on my machine” is a phrase developers use when their code runs correctly on their own computer but fails when deployed to other environments. While “It works on my machine” might help you quickly close a bug report, it does not solve the problem for your end user, and you need to determine what is causing the discrepancies between development and production.

在软件开发中，“在我机器上是好的”是开发者用来描述这种情况的说法：代码在自己电脑上运行正常，但部署到其他环境就失败。虽然“在我机器上是好的”能帮你快速关掉一个 bug 报告，但它并没有为终端用户解决问题；你需要查明是什么导致了开发与生产之间的差异。

The following are variables that can change between environments:

以下是会在不同环境之间变化的变量：

  • Environment differences: Imagine you’ve been developing on your MacBook Pro with 16 GB of RAM, but production runs on Linux servers with different memory constraints. Your local MySQL database might be version 8.0, while production uses PostgreSQL 14. These differences in operating systems, available resources, network configurations, database vendors, and dependency versions can cause code that runs perfectly on your machine to fail spectacularly in production.环境差异：想象你一直在 16 GB 内存的 MacBook Pro 上开发，而生产环境跑在内存约束不同的 Linux 服务器上。你本地的 MySQL 可能是 8.0，而生产用的是 PostgreSQL 14。操作系统、可用资源、网络配置、数据库厂商和依赖版本上的这些差异，会让在你机器上完美运行的代码在生产中惨败。
  • Configuration management: In development, your application might connect to a local database running on your laptop. You might be logging everything to help you debug issues, sending requests to a payment provider’s test API that uses fake credit card numbers. But when you deploy that same code to production, it needs to automatically switch to a secure cloud database, reduce logging to only capture errors, and connect to a real payment processor that charges actual money.配置管理：在开发环境，你的应用可能连的是笔记本电脑上跑的本地数据库。你可能把所有东西都记到日志里以便调试，把请求发给支付提供商的测试 API、用的是假信用卡号。但当你把同一份代码部署到生产时，它需要自动切换到安全的云数据库，把日志降到只记录错误，并接入一个真的会扣钱的真实支付处理方。
  • Concurrency and load: Imagine this scenario: you’ve been testing your shopping cart feature locally by clicking Add to Cart a few times to make sure it works. But on Black Friday, thousands of customers hit that same button simultaneously. Suddenly your database, which handled your solo testing with ease, is overwhelmed by requests. Your server’s memory, which was cruising along at 30% usage, spikes to 95% as it tries to process hundreds of user sessions at once. This is the reality gap between development and production.并发与负载：想象这个场景：你一直在本地测试购物车功能，点几下“加入购物车”确认它能用。但在黑色星期五，成千上万的顾客同时按下那个按钮。突然间，那个轻松应付你单人测试的数据库被请求淹没了。你服务器的内存本来平稳地跑在 30% 使用率，此刻飙升到 95%，因为它要同时处理几百个用户会话。这就是开发与生产之间的现实差距。
  • Data diversity: Your local test database probably has a handful of clean, well-formatted records that you created yourself. Maybe “John Smith” has a perfect phone number like “555-123-4567” and a well-formatted email address. But production tells a different story. Real customer data is messy and unpredictable. Legacy systems might have stored data differently that now breaks validation logic. Then there’s the sheer volume problem. Your test queries run instantly against hundreds of records, but production has millions of customers spanning years of business. This is why testing with realistic, diverse datasets matters. Production data will always have a way of surprising you.数据多样性：你本地的测试数据库里大概只有几条你自己创建的、干净整齐的记录。也许“John Smith”有个完美的电话号码“555-123-4567”和格式规范的邮箱。但生产环境讲的是另一个故事。真实的客户数据又乱又不可预测。遗留系统可能用不同方式存过数据，如今破坏了校验逻辑。还有数据量的问题。你的测试查询对着几百条记录瞬间跑完，而生产环境有跨越多年业务的数百万客户。这就是为什么用真实、多样的数据集做测试很重要。生产数据总有办法让你大吃一惊。
原书第 242 页
  • External dependencies: Modern applications are like team sports: no single player is going to win you the game alone. Your application might handle the user interface, but it passes to a payment processing system to handle payments. It might send requests to an external system for email delivery. It might rely on Google for user authentication. But in production, when one of your “teammates” is having an off day (payment processor is slow, the email service hits rate limits, or the authentication provider goes down), your well-put-together team (application) can still lose the game.外部依赖：现代应用就像团队运动：没有哪个球员能单枪匹马赢下比赛。你的应用可能负责用户界面，但它把支付交给支付处理系统，把发邮件的请求发给外部系统，还可能依赖 Google 做用户认证。但在生产环境，当你的某个“队友”状态不佳（支付处理方很慢、邮件服务触发限流、或认证提供商挂了），你这支配合良好的队伍（应用）仍可能输掉比赛。
  • Security constraints: Production environments are locked down in ways your local machine isn’t. Your laptop might happily accept HTTP requests from anywhere, but production servers sit behind firewalls that block unexpected traffic. Your local API calls work fine over plain HTTP, but production requires HTTPS with valid TLS certificates. That frontend you’re testing locally can freely call your backend, but production enforces CORS policies that might block the same requests. These security layers protect real user data and money, but they can cause your code to fail in production even when it works perfectly on your development machine.安全约束：生产环境的封锁程度是你本地机器比不了的。你的笔记本可能乐呵呵地接受来自任何地方的 HTTP 请求，但生产服务器坐在防火墙后面，会拦截意外流量。你本地的 API 调用用明文 HTTP 好好的，生产却要求带有效 TLS 证书的 HTTPS。你本地测试的前端可以自由调用后端，生产却强制执行 CORS 策略，可能拦截同样的请求。这些安全层保护着真实的用户数据和钱，但它们也可能让你的代码在生产中失败——哪怕它在开发机上完美运行。

To bridge the gap between “works on my machine” and “works in production,” consider the following:

要弥合“在我机器上能跑”和“在生产里能跑”之间的差距，可以考虑以下几点：

  • Containerization: Use tools like Docker to create consistent environments across development and production, eliminating the “but it works on my machine” scenario.容器化：用 Docker 之类的工具在开发和生产之间创建一致的环境，消除“可它在我机器上是好的”这种场景。
  • Observability: Implement comprehensive logging, metrics, and distributed tracing to understand how your application behaves in production and catch issues before they impact users.可观测性：实现全面的日志、指标和分布式追踪，以了解应用在生产中的行为，并在问题影响用户之前捕获它们。
  • Environment parity: Maintain staging environments that closely mirror production, allowing you to catch environment-specific issues early.环境一致性：维护与生产高度一致的预发（staging）环境，让你尽早发现环境特定的问题。
  • Continuous integration and continuous deployment: Practice CI/CD to ensure that your code is regularly tested in production-like conditions. You will learn more about CI/CD later in this chapter.持续集成与持续部署：实践 CI/CD，确保你的代码定期在类生产条件下接受测试。本章后面会更详细地介绍 CI/CD。

Remember, your users don’t care that it works on your machine. They care that it works on theirs. These are the complexities of production and some tips on how to bridge the gap between testing environments and the unpredictability of real users.

记住，你的用户不在乎它在你机器上能不能跑，他们在乎的是在自己机器上能不能跑。以上就是生产环境的复杂性，以及弥合测试环境与真实用户不可预测性之间差距的一些技巧。

In the next section, you’ll learn how to avoid some of these issues by thinking about them throughout the development lifecycle.

下一节中，你将学习如何在整个开发生命周期中提前思考这些问题，从而避免其中一部分。

Building Production-Ready Code

If you’re a parent preparing to send your child off to their first day of school, you have to think about so many details. You wouldn’t just wake them up, hand them their backpack, and push them out the door, would you? Of course not. You’d make sure they’re well-fed, dressed appropriately, have all their supplies, and know how to contact you if something goes wrong. You’d prepare them for the world they’re about to face.

如果你是一位家长，正准备送孩子去上第一天学，你得考虑一大堆细节。你总不会把他们叫醒、递上书包就推出门，对吧？当然不会。你会确保他们吃饱穿暖、带齐所有用品、知道出问题时怎么联系你。你会让他们为即将面对的世界做好准备。

The same applies when preparing your code for production. Your code is your baby, and you need to be certain it’s ready to face the unforeseen challenges of the real world. Just as parents can’t predict every scenario their child might encounter, developers can’t anticipate every possible issue in production. However, with proper preparation, you can give your code the best chance of success by considering performance optimizations, environment-specific configurations, error handling and logging, and security essentials throughout the development process.

为生产环境准备代码时也是一样。你的代码就是你的孩子，你必须确信它已准备好面对真实世界那些不可预见的挑战。正如家长无法预料孩子可能遇到的每一种情形，开发者也无法预料生产中的每一个可能问题。然而，有了恰当的准备，你可以通过在整个开发过程中考虑性能优化、环境特定配置、错误处理与日志、以及安全要点，给代码最好的成功机会。

Performance Optimization

Performance optimization isn’t a dial you simply turn up when you want things to run smoothly. It’s a mindset you need to adopt before writing any code, and it should be an area of your application you constantly review throughout the development process.

性能优化不是一个你想让东西跑顺时拧一下的旋钮。它是一种你在写任何代码之前就需要具备的心态，也应该是你在整个开发过程中不断审视的应用领域。

While performance can indeed be about making your code run faster, ultimately it’s about providing the best possible experience for your users. You can employ several key strategies to improve performance. Think of these as building blocks: you don’t need to implement all of them at once but can gradually incorporate them into your development process:

虽然性能确实可以是让代码跑得更快，但归根结底它是为用户提供最佳体验。你可以采用几种关键策略来提升性能。把它们看作积木：你不需要一次全部实现，可以逐步把它们融入开发过程：

  • Asynchronous programming: Instead of waiting for a task to complete before moving on to the next one (synchronous execution), asynchronous programming allows tasks to run in the background, notifying the main program upon their completion. This is a common solution to this problem, but use it cautiously as it introduces its own complexities and trade-offs.异步编程：异步编程不再是等一个任务完成再进行下一个（同步执行），而是让任务在后台运行，完成时通知主程序。这是解决该问题的常用方案，但要谨慎使用，因为它会引入自身的复杂性和权衡。
  • Reducing network calls: Every request your application makes has a cost associated with it, and the currency is time and resources. Instead of making multiple smaller calls, consider batching them together into a single request.减少网络调用：你的应用发出的每个请求都有成本，货币就是时间和资源。与其发多个小调用，不如考虑把它们合并成一个请求。
  • Caching strategies: If you can identify frequently accessed data that doesn’t change, you can store it in memory or some type of fast storage system. This will reduce database load缓存策略：如果你能识别出频繁访问且不常变化的数据，就可以把它存在内存或某种快速存储系统中。这会降低数据库负载
原书第 244 页

and increase response times. You can learn more about the trade-offs of caching in Chapter 8.

并提升响应速度。关于缓存的权衡，可在第 8 章了解更多。

  • Database query optimization: Use efficient queries, proper indexing, and avoid N + 1 query problems.数据库查询优化：使用高效查询、恰当的索引，避免 N+1 查询问题。
  • Code minification: In modern frontend development, code minification removes unnecessary characters from your code without changing its functionality. Think of it like removing all the spaces and line breaks from a book while keeping all the words: the meaning stays the same, but it takes up less space. Minification removes characters like whitespace, newlines, and comments to make files smaller and faster to download.代码压缩：在现代前端开发中，代码压缩在不改变功能的前提下去除代码中不必要的字符。你可以把它想象成把一本书里所有空格和换行都删掉、却保留所有文字：意思不变，但占的空间更小。压缩会去掉空白符、换行和注释等字符，让文件更小、下载更快。
  • Code bundling: Bundling combines multiple separate code files into fewer, larger files. Instead of your browser downloading 20 separate JavaScript files, it downloads 1 or 2 bundled files. Modern build tools like Webpack or Vite can perform bundling alongside other optimizations like tree shaking (removing unused code) and minification.代码打包：打包把多个独立的代码文件合并成更少、更大的文件。你的浏览器不用下载 20 个独立的 JavaScript 文件，而是下载 1 到 2 个打包文件。Webpack 或 Vite 等现代构建工具可以在打包的同时做其他优化，比如 tree shaking（移除未使用的代码）和压缩。
  • Lazy loading: Load resources (images, code chunks, components) only when they’re actually needed rather than up front. This reduces initial page load time.懒加载：只在真正需要时才加载资源（图片、代码块、组件），而不是一开始就全部加载。这能减少初始页面加载时间。
  • Content delivery networks (CDNs): CDNs complement optimizations like minification and bundling by serving your assets from locations physically closer to your users, which can significantly reduce load times.内容分发网络（CDN）：CDN 通过从物理上离用户更近的位置提供你的静态资源，来补充压缩和打包等优化，从而显著缩短加载时间。

Performance optimization is not just about making code run faster, but about providing the best possible experience for your users. You can do this by changing your mindset and thinking about some of the optimizations you learned about in this section.

性能优化不只是让代码跑得更快，而是为用户提供最佳体验。你可以通过改变心态、思考本节学到的一些优化手段来做到这一点。

Environment-Specific Configurations

You might hear the phrase, “Configuration is code,” but unlike code, configurations vary across environments. Configuration is similar to adjusting your phone’s camera settings for different lighting conditions. Just as settings optimized for bright sunlight might falter in low light, your application needs tailored configurations to perform reliably in each specific environment.

你可能听过“配置即代码”这句话，但与代码不同，配置在不同环境间是变化的。配置就像根据不同光线条件调整手机相机设置。正如为明亮阳光优化的设置在弱光下可能失灵，你的应用也需要量身定制的配置才能在每个特定环境中可靠运行。

Let’s look at a common anti-pattern and its solution. In the following example, the developer has hardcoded the database credentials for their local machine. Instead

让我们看一个常见的反模式及其解决方案。在下面的例子中，开发者把本机的数据库凭据硬编码了。我们应当

原书第 245 页

of hardcoding credentials like this, favor a configuration that can be set for each environment:

避免这样硬编码凭据，转而使用一种可以为每个环境分别设置的配置：

// DON'T DO THIS
public class DbConnection {
   private final String url = "jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/fose";
   private final String username = "admin";
   private final String password = "secret";
}

// DO THIS INSTEAD
public class DbConnection {
   private final String url;
   private final String username;
   private final String password;

   public DbConnection(AppConfiguration config) {
       this.url = config.getDatabaseUrl();
       this.username = config.getDatabaseUsername();
       this.password = config.getDatabasePassword();
   }
}

You just saw an example of hardcoding a database connection string that is specific to a development environment. This doesn’t scale as you move your code into different environments. Here are some more examples of configurations that might change across environments:

你刚看到了一个把开发环境特有的数据库连接字符串硬编码的例子。当你把代码搬到不同环境时，这种做法无法扩展。以下是一些可能在不同环境间变化的配置示例：

  • Logging settings日志设置
  • External service endpoints外部服务端点
  • Database settings数据库设置
  • Cache settings缓存设置
  • Email settings邮件设置
  • Security settings安全设置
  • Feature flags and app behavior特性开关与应用行为

Now that you know that this is something you need to be aware of, let’s look at some ways to configure these items across environments.

既然你知道了这是需要留意的事，我们来看看跨环境配置这些项的几种方式。

Configuration files

We can use configuration files to configure everything from database connection strings to API keys to application-specific settings. While they might be code, they are often human-readable, which makes them appealing. Configuration files also offer you the option to have a file for each environment you are deploying to.

我们可以用配置文件来配置一切——从数据库连接字符串到 API 密钥，再到应用特定的设置。虽然它们可能是代码，但通常是人类可读的，这让它们很有吸引力。配置文件还让你可以为要部署的每个环境各准备一个文件。

In the following example, we define two configuration files: one for development and one for production. This lets you define the properties for each environment:

Environment variables

If you were paying attention to the configuration files in the previous section, you may have noticed some sensitive information in there. Even though these configuration files are specific, they still pose problems. The first problem is that you are exposing sensitive information that will be checked into version control. The other problem is that sensitive information like API keys is usually rotated at scheduled intervals. This means that to change an API key, you will need to redeploy the entire application, which isn’t ideal. In this example, the sensitive information is now defined in an environment variable and is no longer hardcoded:

如果你留意了上一节的配置文件，可能会注意到里面有一些敏感信息。即便这些配置文件是环境特定的，它们仍然有问题。第一个问题是，你把会被提交到版本控制的敏感信息暴露了出来。另一个问题是，像 API 密钥这样的敏感信息通常会按计划定期轮换。这意味着要更换一个 API 密钥，你得重新部署整个应用，并不理想。在下面的例子中，敏感信息现在定义在环境变量里，不再硬编码：

# application-prod.yaml
services:
 service1:
   url: ${SERVICE1_URL}
   api-key: ${SERVICE1_API_KEY}

Feature flags

Feature flags (also known as feature toggles) are a software development technique that allows developers to enable or disable features at runtime without deploying new code. Consider them like a control panel for your application’s features.

特性开关（也称 feature toggle）是一种软件开发技术，允许开发者在运行时启用或禁用特性，而无需部署新代码。你可以把它想象成应用特性的控制面板。

原书第 247 页

Feature flags offer several benefits for both your development teams and your users. You can ship code to production while keeping features hidden from users, allowing for safer deployments and better separation of code releases from feature releases. They enable gradual rollouts to specific user groups, letting you test features with a subset of users before full deployment. Feature flags also make A/B testing straightforward by allowing you to compare different user experiences, and they provide the ability to quickly roll back features without requiring a code deployment.

特性开关为开发团队和用户都带来若干好处。你可以把代码发布到生产，同时对用户隐藏特性，从而实现更安全的部署，并把代码发布与特性发布更好地分离。它们支持向特定用户群逐步灰度发布，让你在全量部署之前先在一小部分用户身上测试特性。特性开关还让 A/B 测试变得直截了当——你可以比较不同的用户体验，还能快速回滚特性而无需部署代码。

There are three common types of feature flags to consider. Release flags help you hide incomplete features in production, keeping your main branch deployable while work continues. Experiment flags are designed for comparing user experiences and gathering data on user behavior. Permission flags control feature access based on user roles or subscription levels, making them useful for tiered product offerings.

有三种常见的特性开关类型值得考虑。发布开关帮你在生产中隐藏未完成的特性，让主干分支在继续开发的同时始终可部署。实验开关用于比较用户体验、收集用户行为数据。权限开关根据用户角色或订阅等级控制特性访问，适合分层的产品套餐。

Feature Flag Hygiene
特性开关的卫生

Feature flags should be regularly reviewed and cleaned up. Temporary flags that become permanent create unnecessary complexity in your codebase. Establish a cleanup schedule that works well for your team and set expiration dates when creating new feature flags. Create documentation that clearly states the purpose and expected lifespan of each flag.
特性开关应当定期评审和清理。临时开关变成永久开关会在代码库中制造不必要的复杂性。建立一个适合你团队的清理计划，并在创建新特性开关时设置到期日。编写文档，清楚说明每个开关的用途和预期寿命。

Secrets

Secrets are sensitive configuration values like API keys, passwords, and tokens that require special care. Managing secrets properly is crucial for application security and requires following several important practices.

机密（secret）是像 API 密钥、密码和令牌这样的敏感配置值，需要特别小心。妥善管理机密对应用安全至关重要，需要遵守若干重要实践。

Never store secrets directly in your code or commit them to version control. This security violation can cost you money and damage user trust. If you do commit these to version control, it will require you to rewrite Git history, which can be a complex process. Additionally, sharing source code with third parties becomes a significant security risk when secrets are embedded in the codebase.

永远不要把机密直接存在代码里，也不要提交到版本控制。这种安全违规可能让你付出金钱代价并损害用户信任。如果你真把它们提交进了版本控制，就得重写 Git 历史，那可能是个复杂过程。此外，当机密嵌在代码库中时，与第三方共享源代码会变成重大安全风险。

Instead, use dedicated secrets management services like AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, or Azure Key Vault. These services provide secure storage, encryption, and access controls specifically designed for sensitive data. Make credential rotation a regular practice, ideally automated through your secrets management platform. This limits the window of vulnerability if credentials are ever compromised.

相反，应使用专门的机密管理服务，如 AWS Secrets Manager、HashiCorp Vault 或 Azure Key Vault。这些服务提供专为敏感数据设计的安全存储、加密和访问控制。把凭据轮换作为常规实践，最好通过机密管理平台自动化。这能在凭据万一泄露时缩小受攻击的时间窗口。

Access to production secrets should be strictly controlled and limited to team members who absolutely need it. Use the principle of least privilege and implement proper authentication and authorization controls. Finally, maintain separate secrets for each environment the application gets published to. Development, staging, and production should never share the same credentials. This isolation prevents accidentally exposing production environments during development and testing.

对生产机密的访问应严格控制，仅限于绝对需要的团队成员。使用最小权限原则，实现恰当的认证和授权控制。最后，为应用发布到的每个环境维护各自独立的机密。开发、预发和生产绝不应共享同一套凭据。这种隔离能防止在开发和测试过程中意外暴露生产环境。

As you can see, there are a number of things to remember when configuring your application for multiple environments. The next consideration for building production-ready code is to employ proper error handling and logging to catch issues when they arise.

如你所见，为多环境配置应用时有不少事情要记住。构建可上线代码的下一个考虑点，是采用恰当的错误处理和日志，在问题出现时捕获它们。

Error Handling and Logging

As you have already learned, the world of production can be an unpredictable place. Murphy’s law reminds us that if something can go wrong, it will go wrong. In this unforgiving environment, proper error handling and logging are not just good practices; they are essential survival skills for production applications. They enable us to catch issues before they cascade into system-wide failures and provide critical insights when solving the problems that will inevitably arise.

正如你已经了解的，生产世界可能是个不可预测的地方。墨菲定律提醒我们：凡是可能出错的事，终将出错。在这个无情的环境中，恰当的错误处理和日志不只是良好实践，而是生产应用的必备生存技能。它们让我们在问题级联成系统范围的故障之前捕获它，并在解决那些不可避免会出现的问题时提供关键洞见。

When you begin building out a new feature, it’s natural to focus on the “happy path.” This is the ideal scenario your users take where everything works perfectly. However, in the real world of software development, this represents only a small portion of what you need to consider. Following the Pareto principle, while the happy path might represent 20% of your code, handling edge cases and errors often accounts for 80% of your time and effort. This is where you’ll spend most of your development time and where experienced developers distinguish themselves.

当你开始构建一个新特性时，自然会聚焦在“快乐路径”上。这是用户走的理想场景——一切完美运行。然而在软件开发的真实世界里，这只占你需要考虑内容的一小部分。按照帕累托法则，快乐路径可能只占你代码的 20%，而处理边缘情况和错误往往占去你 80% 的时间和精力。这正是你开发时间的主要去处，也是资深开发者脱颖而出的地方。

Error handling

So what does effective error handling actually look like in practice? Here are some concrete strategies you’ll use regularly:

那么，有效的错误处理在实践中到底长什么样？以下是一些你会经常用到的具体策略：

  • Graceful degradation: When a feature fails, provide a simplified version instead of breaking entirely. For example, if your weather API is down, show cached weather data with a note that it might be outdated rather than displaying an error page.优雅降级：当一个特性失败时，提供一个简化版本而不是彻底崩溃。例如，如果你的天气 API 挂了，就显示缓存的天气数据并注明可能已过期，而不是显示一个错误页面。
  • Meaningful error messages: Replace technical jargon with user-friendly language. Instead of “Database connection failed,” tell users “We’re having trouble loading your data right now. Please try again in a few minutes.”有意义的错误信息：用用户友好的语言替换技术黑话。不要说“数据库连接失败”，而要告诉用户：“我们现在加载数据遇到了点麻烦，请几分钟后再试。”
  • Logging for debugging: Record what went wrong behind the scenes so you can fix it later. Log the technical details (like error codes and stack traces) that help developers, while showing users only what they need to know.用于调试的日志：在幕后记录出了什么问题，以便日后修复。记录帮助开发者的技术细节（如错误码和堆栈跟踪），而向用户只展示他们需要知道的。
  • Fallback options: Always have a Plan B. If your primary payment processor fails during checkout, automatically switch to a backup processor so customers can still complete their purchases.兜底选项：永远要有 B 计划。如果主支付处理方在结账时失败，自动切换到备用处理方，让顾客仍能完成购买。

Logging

Effective logging provides insight into production issues. The challenge lies in striking the right balance. Insufficient logging can leave you in the dark, while excessive logging can create noise that obscures crucial information.

有效的日志能让你洞察生产中的问题。挑战在于把握恰当的平衡。日志不足会让你两眼一抹黑，而日志过多又会制造噪音、掩盖关键信息。

While the implementations might vary across programming languages the concept of logging levels is common. Here are the logging levels in Java that help developers categorize and filter log messages based on their severity and importance:

虽然不同编程语言的实现可能不同，但日志级别这个概念是共通的。以下是 Java 中的日志级别，它们帮助开发者根据严重程度和重要性对日志消息进行分类和过滤：

  • ERROR: Use for serious issues that need immediate attentionERROR：用于需要立即处理的严重问题
  • WARN: For potentially harmful situationsWARN：用于潜在有害的情况
  • INFO: Normal business process eventsINFO：正常的业务流程事件
  • DEBUG: Detailed information for debuggingDEBUG：用于调试的详细信息

When logging, try not to be too verbose. Focus on the critical items. You should not log the following:

记日志时，尽量不要太啰嗦。聚焦关键项。你不应该记录以下内容：

  • Sensitive information, such as passwords, API keys, authentication tokens, or secrets.敏感信息，如密码、API 密钥、认证令牌或机密。
  • Personally identifiable information (PII). You will learn more about this later in this chapter.个人身份信息（PII）。本章后面会详细介绍。
  • Large objects or entire response payloads. Instead, log meaningful information that will help identify the issue at hand.大对象或整个响应负载。相反，记录有助于定位当前问题的有意义信息。
  • Duplicate logging of the same information across multiple layers of your application.在应用多个层级重复记录同一信息。

As you just learned, error handling and logging are vital to getting visibility when things go wrong in production. Another important aspect of building production-ready code is making sure that it is secure.

如你刚学到的，错误处理和日志对于在生产出问题时获得可见性至关重要。构建可上线代码的另一个重要方面，是确保它是安全的。

Security Essentials

Security isn’t something you think about once and move on with your life. It is an ongoing process that requires vigilance and regular attention. As you deploy applications to production, remember that security should be built into your development process from the start, not bolted on at the end. While you don’t need to be a security expert, understanding these fundamentals will help you build more secure applications and make you a more valuable team member. One really good resource

安全不是你想一次就完事的事。它是一个持续的过程，需要警惕和常态化的关注。当你把应用部署到生产时，记住：安全应当从一开始就内建到开发过程中，而不是最后才拧上去。虽然你不需要成为安全专家，但理解这些基础会帮你构建更安全的应用，让你成为更有价值的团队成员。一个非常好的学习资源

for learning about web application security is the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP). OWASP provides free, practical security guidance that’s widely trusted by developers worldwide. In this section, you will learn some ways you can make your applications more secure.

是学习 Web 应用安全的开放 Web 应用安全项目（OWASP）。OWASP 提供免费、实用的安全指引，受到全球开发者的广泛信赖。在本节中，你将学到一些让应用更安全的方法。

Securing communication with HTTPS

While you’re developing locally you might be inclined to use Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) because it’s frankly just more convenient. However, it is important to test with HTTP Secure (HTTPS) before deploying to production. There are tools that allow you to create trusted certifications for local development.

在本地开发时，你可能倾向于使用超文本传输协议（HTTP），因为坦白说它就是更方便。然而，在部署到生产之前用 HTTPS 测试很重要。有一些工具可以让你为本地开发创建受信任的证书。

There are certain messages that can be seen by anyone, and there are messages that you want only the recipient to see. Imagine a postcard you send to someone while you’re on vacation. The postcard has a picture of the beach on the front and on the back a handwritten message for anyone to see. This is what it is like to send data over HTTP. HTTP transfers plain text data between your browser and the server. Any sensitive information like passwords, credit card numbers, secrets, or personal data is visible to anyone who intercepts the traffic.

有些消息谁都能看，有些消息你只想让收件人看到。想象你度假时寄给别人的明信片：正面是海滩照片，背面是手写的留言，谁都能看。这就是通过 HTTP 发送数据的样子。HTTP 在浏览器和服务器之间传输明文数据。任何敏感信息——密码、信用卡号、机密或个人数据——对任何拦截流量的人都是可见的。

If you want to keep your vacation message private, you would put it inside a sealed envelope; this is what HTTPS does for you. HTTPS adds a layer of encryption using Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocols.

如果你想让度假留言保持私密，就会把它装进封好的信封里；这就是 HTTPS 为你做的事。HTTPS 使用传输层安全（TLS）协议加了一层加密。

TLS certificates are like digital ID cards for websites. When you visit an HTTPS site, the server presents its certificate to prove its identity. These certificates are issued by trusted certificate authorities (CAs) who verify the website owner’s identity. Once your browser verifies the certificate, TLS uses this trusted connection to set up strong encryption for all data transfer. This encryption ensures that your information can’t be read by prying eyes and also means that the information can’t be modified while it’s being transmitted between your browser and the server.

TLS 证书就像网站的数字身份证。当你访问一个 HTTPS 站点时，服务器出示证书来证明身份。这些证书由受信任的证书颁发机构（CA）颁发，它们会验证网站所有者的身份。一旦浏览器验证了证书，TLS 就用这条受信任的连接为所有数据传输建立强加密。这种加密确保你的信息不被窥探者读取，也意味着信息在浏览器与服务器之间传输时无法被篡改。

SSL vs. TLS
SSL 与 TLS

While Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) is an older protocol that TLS has replaced, many people still use the term “SSL” out of habit. SSL has known security vulnerabilities and should not be used in production applications. When someone refers to SSL today, they usually mean TLS, but it’s important to verify that systems are actually using TLS protocols.
虽然安全套接层（SSL）是已被 TLS 取代的旧协议，但许多人出于习惯仍使用“SSL”这个说法。SSL 有已知的安全漏洞，不应在生产应用中使用。如今有人提到 SSL 时，他们通常指的是 TLS，但重要的是要核实系统确实在用 TLS 协议。
原书第 251 页

HTTPS isn’t going to fix all of your security problems. It is one layer of security that you should be thinking of as you take your applications to production. Here are some best practices you can follow:

HTTPS 不会解决你所有的安全问题。它是你把应用推向生产时应当考虑的一层安全。以下是一些可以遵循的最佳实践：

  • Use HTTPS everywhere, not just for login pages.到处使用 HTTPS，而不只是登录页。
  • Redirect HTTP to HTTPS automatically.自动把 HTTP 重定向到 HTTPS。
  • Keep certificates up-to-date (consider using automated certificate management tools).保持证书最新（考虑使用自动化证书管理工具）。
  • Use secure TLS versions (1.2 or higher).使用安全的 TLS 版本（1.2 或更高）。

Authentication best practices

Security breaches can cause a lot of problems within your organization, like exposing sensitive data, damaging customer trust, and potentially resulting in significant financial and reputational losses. Proper authentication is a good defense against these threats.

安全泄露会在你的组织内造成大量问题，比如暴露敏感数据、损害客户信任，并可能导致重大的财务和声誉损失。恰当的认证是抵御这些威胁的良好防线。

Authentication is the process of verifying that users are who they claim to be, while authorization determines what verified users are allowed to do. The first and most important rule is: never, under any circumstances, create your own security measures. While crafting your own authentication systems might seem straightforward, security experts have spent decades identifying and mitigating complex vulnerabilities that aren’t always obvious.

认证（authentication）是验证用户是否如其所声称身份的过程，而授权（authorization）决定已验证的用户可以做什么。第一条也是最重要的规则是：无论如何，永远不要自己造安全措施。虽然自己设计认证系统看起来直截了当，但安全专家已经花了几十年去识别和缓解那些并不总是显而易见的复杂漏洞。

Spring Security in the Java world represents over 20 years of security work. It offers proven solutions for common security problems like password storage. It includes password encoders that prevent storing passwords as plain text, which is very dangerous. In the following example, we create a new BCryptPasswordEncoder, which will be used to encode passwords:

Java 世界的 Spring Security 凝聚了 20 多年的安全工作。它为密码存储等常见安全问题提供了经过验证的解决方案。它内置了密码编码器，防止以明文存储密码——那非常危险。在下面的例子中，我们创建一个新的 BCryptPasswordEncoder，它将用于编码密码：

@Bean
public PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder() {
    return new BCryptPasswordEncoder();
}

And then use that password encoder to encode the password before saving it off to a database:

然后在把密码存入数据库之前，用这个密码编码器对它进行编码：

// Create new user entity
User user = new User();
user.setUsername(registrationDto.getUsername());
user.setEmail(registrationDto.getEmail());

// Encode the password before saving
user.setPassword(passwordEncoder.encode(registrationDto.getPassword()));
// Save and return the new user
return userRepository.save(user);

Authentication is a vital component to application security, serving as the first line of defense against unauthorized access. Let’s explore the building blocks of a robust authentication system.

认证是应用安全的关键组成部分，是抵御未授权访问的第一道防线。让我们看看一个健壮认证系统的构成要素。

Strong password management is essential for protecting your systems against unauthorized access. For example, enforce passwords with a minimum of 12 characters, combining uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters. Check against databases of common or compromised passwords and prevent users from reusing previous passwords. Use modern hashing algorithms with unique salts for each password. A salt is random data added before hashing to prevent rainbow table attacks. Encourage and support the use of password managers with auto-fill capability.

强密码管理对于保护系统免受未授权访问至关重要。例如，强制密码至少 12 个字符，组合大写、小写、数字和特殊字符。对照常见或已泄露密码库进行检查，防止用户复用旧密码。使用现代哈希算法，并为每个密码使用独特的盐（salt）。盐是哈希前加入的随机数据，用于防止彩虹表攻击。鼓励并支持使用带自动填充功能的密码管理器。

Even with all these technical protections in place, remember that passwords ultimately depend on human behavior. The strongest password policy won’t help if users write passwords on sticky notes or share them with colleagues. This is why implementing multiple layers of security (like multifactor authentication, covered later) is so important.

即便有了所有这些技术防护，也要记住密码最终取决于人的行为。如果用户把密码写在便利贴上或与同事分享，最强的密码策略也无济于事。这就是为什么实现多层安全（比如后面会讲的多因素认证）如此重要。

Securing user accounts requires multiple layers of defense against unauthorized access attempts. For example, implement exponential backoff for failed login attempts, starting with short delays like 5 seconds and gradually increasing to 30 minutes or more. Track failed attempts across multiple accounts from the same IP address and monitor when single accounts are being targeted from multiple locations. Add CAPTCHA after several failed attempts to prevent automated attacks, and alert users when login attempts occur from new devices or unfamiliar locations. Finally, implement secure account recovery flows with appropriate verification steps to help legitimate users regain access while keeping attackers out.

保护用户账户需要多层防御来抵御未授权访问尝试。例如，对失败的登录尝试实施指数退避：从 5 秒这样的短延迟开始，逐渐增加到 30 分钟甚至更久。追踪来自同一 IP 对多个账户的失败尝试，并监控单个账户是否正被从多个地点盯上。数次失败尝试后加入验证码以防止自动化攻击；当从新设备或陌生地点登录时提醒用户。最后，实现带恰当验证步骤的安全账户恢复流程，帮助合法用户重新获得访问权，同时把攻击者挡在外面。

Effective session management protects users while they interact with your system and prevents unauthorized access to active sessions. Use cryptographically secure tokens with sufficient entropy to ensure that sessions cannot be easily guessed or hijacked. Implement both idle and absolute session timeouts. For instance, automatically log users out after 30 minutes of inactivity or 8 hours total, with shorter timeouts for sensitive operations like banking. Maintain a blocklist of revoked tokens until their natural expiration to prevent reuse of compromised sessions.

有效的会话管理在用户与系统交互时保护他们，并防止对活动会话的未授权访问。使用加密安全、熵足够高的令牌，确保会话不易被猜测或劫持。同时实现空闲超时和绝对超时。例如，不活动 30 分钟或累计 8 小时后自动登出，对银行这类敏感操作使用更短的超时。维护一份已撤销令牌的黑名单，直到其自然过期，以防被泄露的会话被复用。

Adding multiple layers of verification strengthens your authentication security beyond just passwords. Support multiple authentication methods like authenticator apps, security keys, and biometrics to give users options that work for their situation. While SMS and email are convenient and widely used, be aware they are more vulnerable to attacks such as SIM swapping.

加入多层验证能把认证安全从仅仅依赖密码提升上来。支持多种认证方式，如验证器应用、安全密钥和生物识别，让用户能选择适合自己情况的方式。虽然短信和邮件方便且被广泛使用，但要注意它们更容易受到 SIM 交换等攻击。

You can trigger additional verification based on unusual behavior. For example, require extra authentication when users log in from new locations or devices. Require MFA during account recovery processes to prevent attackers from bypassing your

你可以基于异常行为触发额外验证。例如，当用户从新地点或新设备登录时要求额外认证。在账户恢复流程中要求 MFA，以防攻击者绕过你的

security. Provide secure backup codes so users are not locked out when their primary MFA method is unavailable. Consider allowing trusted device caching with appropriate security controls so users are not constantly challenged on their regular devices.

安全。提供安全的备用验证码，让用户在主要 MFA 方式不可用时不会被锁在外面。考虑在恰当的安全控制下允许受信任设备缓存，这样用户在常用设备上不会被反复盘问。

Safeguarding user data

Your users are trusting you with their data, and you have both a professional and ethical responsibility to protect that trust. Beyond legal requirements, respecting user privacy and data security is simply the right thing to do. Your decisions as a developer can genuinely impact people’s lives, financial security, and personal safety.

你的用户把数据托付给你，你在职业上和道德上都有责任保护这份信任。除了法律要求之外，尊重用户隐私和数据安全本来就是该做的事。作为开发者，你的决策真的会影响人们的生活、财务安全和人身安全。

When you start building applications that handle user data, you will most likely come across the term personally identifiable information (PII). This type of data can include obvious details like a name and social security number but also less obvious ones like IP addresses or device identifiers. Some data is considered PII when it is combined with other data.

当你开始构建处理用户数据的应用时，很可能会遇到“个人身份信息”（PII）这个术语。这类数据既包括姓名、社保号这样显而易见的细节，也包括 IP 地址或设备标识符这样不那么明显的。有些数据在与其他数据结合时才被视为 PII。

One way to start thinking about this in development is by marking data as sensitive. In the following example, written in Java, a custom annotation marks data as PII. Within that custom annotation, you can use various masking methods:

在开发中开始考虑这一点的一种方式，是把数据标记为敏感。在下面这个 Java 例子中，用一个自定义注解把数据标记为 PII。在那个自定义注解里，你可以使用各种脱敏方法：

public class UserProfile {
   private String userId;
   private String hashedPassword;
   @Sensitive  // Custom annotation to mark PII
   private String email;
   @Sensitive
   private String phoneNumber;
   @Sensitive
   private LocalDate dob;
}

Encryption: Your last line of defense

What happens when you have sensitive data like financial information (credit cards, bank account numbers, tax returns, etc.) and you need to store it in a database? This is information you absolutely should not store in plain text. While in development, you should start thinking of encryption and consider it your safety net. Think of it as a secure vault: even if someone breaks in, they can’t use what they find without the key.

当你有金融信息（信用卡、银行账号、报税表等）这样的敏感数据、又需要存进数据库时，会发生什么？这类信息你绝对不该明文存储。在开发阶段，你就应当开始考虑加密，把它当作你的安全网。把它想象成一个保险库：即使有人闯入，没有钥匙也用不了他找到的东西。

The following class provides a secure method for encrypting sensitive data in Java. It uses the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), a highly secure encryption algorithm that provides both confidentiality and data integrity protection. When implementing AES, you’ll need to choose a key length—currently 128 bits provides strong security for most applications, though many developers are moving to 256-bit keys for future-proofing against advancing computing power:

下面这个类在 Java 中提供了一种加密敏感数据的安全方法。它使用高级加密标准（AES），一种高度安全的加密算法，同时提供机密性和数据完整性保护。实现 AES 时，你需要选择密钥长度——目前 128 位对大多数应用已提供强安全，不过许多开发者正转向 256 位密钥，以应对不断增长的计算能力、面向未来：

原书第 254 页
class DataEncryptionService {
  private final SecretKey key;
  DataEncryptionService(SecretKey key) { this.key = key; }

  String encrypt(String s) throws GeneralSecurityException {
    byte[] iv = new byte[12]; new SecureRandom().nextBytes(iv);
    Cipher c = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding");
    c.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, key, new GCMParameterSpec(128, iv));
    byte[] ct = c.doFinal(s.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    byte[] out = ByteBuffer.allocate(iv.length + ct.length)
                 .put(iv).put(ct).array();
    return Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(out); // encodes IV||ciphertext
  }
}

Compliance requirements

Software compliance means following specific rules, standards, and regulations. This includes both internal company policies and external legal requirements. As you write code, keep these compliance practices in mind:

软件合规意味着遵守特定的规则、标准和法规。这既包括公司内部政策，也包括外部法律要求。写代码时，请牢记以下合规实践：

  • Start with privacy by design: build data protection in your systems from the beginning.从设计上的隐私开始：从一开始就把数据保护内建到系统中。
  • Apply secure coding standards in your daily work.在日常工作中应用安全编码标准。
  • Implement proper data encryption for sensitive data both in transit and at rest:对传输中（in transit）和静态（at rest）的敏感数据都实施恰当的数据加密：
    • In transit: Use HTTPS for all data transmission (this protects data while traveling between user and server).传输中：所有数据传输使用 HTTPS（这保护数据在用户与服务器之间传输时的安全）。
    • At rest: Encrypt sensitive data stored in your database (this protects data even if someone gains database access).静态：加密数据库中存储的敏感数据（即使有人获得数据库访问权，也能保护数据）。
    • Be extra cautious when decrypting data in server memory, as skilled attackers might find ways to access it there.在服务器内存中解密数据时要格外小心，因为老练的攻击者可能会设法在那里访问它。
  • Create clear mechanisms for data deletion and export requests.为数据删除和导出请求创建清晰的机制。
  • Document all interactions with sensitive information.记录所有与敏感信息的交互。

You don’t need to memorize every regulation but recognize when your code touches regulated data and ask for help from someone on your team. Security is a team effort. While you’ll implement secure best practices, your organization’s security professionals should be involved in design decisions from the start of each project. As a developer, you won’t always recognize when you’re approaching something that could create security risks, and that’s normal.

你不需要背下每一条法规，但要能识别你的代码何时触及受监管的数据，并向团队中懂行的人求助。安全是团队的事。虽然你会落实安全最佳实践，但公司的安全专业人员应当从每个项目一开始就参与设计决策。作为开发者，你并不总能识别自己正在接近可能造成安全风险的东西——这很正常。

Remember that security is about layers. No single security measure is perfect, but implementing multiple layers of security makes it significantly harder for attackers to compromise your system. This is something you need to be thinking about during the development process, so try to layer on security to get into a good practice of being security conscious.

Deployment Pipeline

A deployment pipeline is your roadmap for safely and reliably moving your code from one environment to production. Think of it as a well-oiled assembly line where each component plays a specific role in transforming your code into a running application that real users can access.

部署流水线是你把代码安全、可靠地从一个环境搬到生产环境的路线图。把它想象成一条运转良好的装配线，每个组件都扮演特定角色，把你的代码变成真实用户可以访问的运行中应用。

Your deployment pipeline consists of four interconnected components that work together like gears in a machine:

你的部署流水线由四个相互关联的组件构成，像机器里的齿轮一样协同工作：

  • Deployment environments: These are the stages where your code will live and run, from your local development setup to the production servers where customers interact with your application. Each environment serves a specific purpose in validating your code before it reaches users.部署环境：这是你的代码栖身和运行的各个阶段，从你本地的开发环境，到客户与应用交互的生产服务器。每个环境在代码到达用户之前都承担特定的验证目的。
  • Version control strategies: Coordinates how multiple developers contribute changes to the same codebase without stepping on each other’s toes. These strategies become your safety net for managing releases and handling emergencies.版本控制策略：协调多个开发者如何向同一代码库贡献改动而不互相踩脚。这些策略成为你管理发布和处理紧急情况的安全网。

  • Deployment automation: Eliminates the manual, error-prone steps of moving code between environments. Instead of following a checklist and hoping you don’t miss anything, automation ensures that the same reliable process runs every time.部署自动化：消除在环境之间搬代码时手动、易错的步骤。自动化确保每次都跑同一套可靠流程，而不是照着清单做、盼着别漏什么。
  • CI/CD (continuous integration and continuous deployment): Ties everything together by automatically moving your code through the pipeline—from the moment you commit changes to when they’re running in production.CI/CD（持续集成与持续部署）：把一切串起来，自动让你的代码流过流水线——从你提交改动那一刻，到它们在生产中运行。

By the end of this chapter, you’ll understand how these pieces fit together to create a deployment process that’s both reliable and stress-free.

学完本章，你会理解这些部分如何拼在一起，形成一个既可靠又无压力的部署流程。

Deployment Environments

Before you can grasp the deployment process within your company, it’s crucial to understand the environments that you will be deploying code to. These will vary across organizations and even among teams within the same organization. Here is a list of common environments you might find and their purposes:

在你理解公司的部署流程之前，关键是要理解你要把代码部署到哪些环境。这些环境在不同组织间、甚至同一组织的不同团队间都会不同。以下是你可能遇到的常见环境及其用途：

  • Local development: This is your local playground where your coding journey begins. While it’s your personal workspace for experimentation, remember that your fellow developers share a similar setup.本地开发：这是你开始编码之旅的本地游乐场。虽然这是你个人实验的工作空间，但记住其他开发者也有类似的环境。
  • Testing/QA: Although you hopefully have a comprehensive test suite to run locally, the testing environment is your first shared checkpoint. This is where quality assurance takes place, and your test suite might behave differently than it does locally.测试/QA：虽然你希望本地就有一套全面的测试套件，但测试环境是第一个共享检查点。质量保证在这里进行，你的测试套件在这里的表现可能与本地不同。
  • Staging: Think of staging as the dress rehearsal for the big show. It’s a production-like environment that serves as the final testing ground before going live. This is ideal for performance testing and user acceptance testing.预发（staging）：把预发想象成正式演出前的带妆彩排。它是一个类生产环境，作为上线前最后的测试场。它非常适合性能测试和用户验收测试。
  • Production: This is the main stage and your ultimate goal. Here, real users will interact with the application you’ve invested so much time and energy in creating.生产：这是主舞台，也是你的终极目标。在这里，真实用户将与你投入大量时间精力构建的应用交互。

Earlier in this chapter, you learned about configuration management. A crucial part of moving an application between environments is ensuring correct configuration for each stage. Configuration management should be an integral part of your deployment process, not an afterthought. To understand how to move code from one environment to the next, you must understand what will change between those environments.

本章前面你学过配置管理。在环境之间移动应用的一个关键部分，是确保每个阶段都有正确的配置。配置管理应当是部署流程中不可或缺的一部分，而不是事后才想起。要理解如何把代码从一个环境搬到下一个，你必须理解那些环境之间会有什么变化。

Version Control Strategies

Version control strategies become especially important in production environments where code stability, reliability, and deployment efficiency are critical. In production, these strategies enable teams to manage feature releases without disrupting live services, quickly address problematic deployments (either by rolling back to a previous version or rolling forward with a fix), and maintain detailed audit trails for compliance purposes.

在代码稳定性、可靠性和部署效率至关重要的生产环境中，版本控制策略变得尤为重要。在生产中，这些策略让团队能够管理特性发布而不中断线上服务，快速处理有问题的部署（要么回滚到先前版本，要么带着修复向前滚动），并为合规目的维护详细的审计轨迹。

Through education or work, you likely have some experience with version control. You’ve probably used it in personal projects and have a good understanding of basic Git concepts like cloning repositories, adding and removing files, and pushing changes. This foundation is great for getting started, but as you move into an organizational setting, the introduction of teams brings new complexities to version control. The following are popular workflows for handling these issues:

通过学习或工作，你大概已经有一些版本控制经验。你可能在个人项目里用过它，对克隆仓库、增删文件、推送改动等 Git 基本概念有不错的理解。这个基础对于入门来说很好，但当你进入组织环境，团队的引入给版本控制带来了新的复杂性。以下是处理这些问题的流行工作流：

  • Git Flow: Uses multiple long-lived branches to separate different types of work (features, releases, hotfixes). This provides strong isolation between development and production code. We’ll take a closer look at Git Flow in this section.Git Flow：使用多个长期分支来分离不同类型的工作（特性、发布、热修复）。这在开发代码和生产代码之间提供了强隔离。本节我们会更仔细地看 Git Flow。
  • GitHub Flow: A simpler approach that uses just a main branch and short-lived feature branches. Changes go directly from feature branches to production after review.GitHub Flow：一种更简单的方式，只用一个 main 分支和短期的特性分支。改动经过评审后直接从特性分支进入生产。
  • Trunk-based development: Emphasizes frequent integration where all developers work on a single main branch with very short-lived feature branches (often less than a day).基于主干的开发：强调频繁集成，所有开发者在单一 main 分支上工作，特性分支非常短命（通常不到一天）。
  • Release train: Coordinates regular, scheduled releases (like weekly or monthly) where features are bundled together for deployment.发布火车：协调定期、计划好的发布（如每周或每月），把特性打包在一起部署。

Let’s explore Git Flow because its clear structure makes it excellent for understanding how teams collaborate with version control. This branching strategy organizes work by using different types of branches, each with a specific purpose. Some of the branches will remain throughout the lifecycle of the project, while others will exist only long enough to complete a particular task.

让我们探究 Git Flow，因为它清晰的结构非常适合理解团队如何用版本控制协作。这种分支策略通过使用不同类型的分支来组织工作，每种分支都有特定目的。有些分支会在项目整个生命周期中存在，另一些则只存在到完成某个特定任务为止。

We’ll explore each type of branch and learn how teams work together without stepping on one another’s toes.

我们将探究每种分支类型，了解团队如何协作而不互相踩脚。

Core branches

Git Flow is built around two core, long-running branches that form the foundation of your project.

Git Flow 围绕两个核心的、长期运行的分支构建，它们构成项目的基础。

原书第 259 页

The main branch represents your production-ready code. It is your source of truth. This branch should always be stable and deployable. When working in a team:

main 分支代表你可上线的代码。它是你的事实来源。这个分支应当始终稳定、可部署。团队协作时：

  • Keep the main branch protected from direct commits: In Git Flow, the main branch receives code that has already been reviewed and tested through the develop branch, so protection here focuses on preventing accidental direct commits rather than code review.保护 main 分支，禁止直接提交：在 Git Flow 中，main 分支接收的是已经通过 develop 分支评审和测试过的代码，所以这里的保护重点是防止意外的直接提交，而非代码评审。
  • Ensure that the main branch passes all automated tests: Automated testing is your safety net for detecting problems before they reach production.确保 main 分支通过所有自动化测试：自动化测试是你的安全网，在问题到达生产之前发现它们。

main vs. master
main 与 master

The main branch was traditionally called master, but many organizations now use main to adopt more inclusive terminology. Both terms refer to the same concept.
main 分支传统上叫 master，但许多组织现在改用 main 以采用更具包容性的术语。两个术语指的是同一个概念。

The develop branch is where the day-to-day action happens in Git Flow. Think of it as your team’s shared workspace, where individual features come together before they’re ready for production.

develop 分支是 Git Flow 中日常活动发生的地方。把它想象成团队的共享工作区，各个特性在准备好上生产之前在这里汇合。

When working with the develop branch:

使用 develop 分支时：

  • Protect the develop branch with code review requirements: This is where code review actually happens in Git Flow. When feature branches merge into develop, team members review changes, catch issues, and ensure coding standards.用代码评审要求保护 develop 分支：这才是 Git Flow 中真正发生代码评审的地方。当特性分支合并进 develop 时，团队成员评审改动、发现问题、确保编码规范。
  • Keep the develop branch always buildable: While it may contain incomplete features, the code should always compile and pass basic tests.保持 develop 分支始终可构建：虽然它可能包含未完成的特性，但代码应当始终能编译并通过基本测试。
  • Test integration regularly: Since develop contains multiple features being worked on simultaneously, run your full test suite frequently to catch integration issues early.定期测试集成：由于 develop 包含多个同时开发的特性，要频繁运行完整测试套件，尽早发现集成问题。

The develop branch acts as a staging area where features are tested together before being packaged into a release and ultimately merged to main.

develop 分支充当一个集水区，特性在这里一起测试，然后才被打包成发布版、最终合并到 main。

Supporting branches

Besides the core branches, Git Flow uses temporary, short-lived branches for specific tasks. These supporting branches help keep work organized and prevent conflicts among team members.

除了核心分支，Git Flow 还为特定任务使用临时的、短期的分支。这些辅助分支帮助保持工作有序，防止团队成员之间的冲突。

原书第 260 页

Feature branches are where you’ll spend most of your development time. When you start working on a new feature or bugfix, you create a dedicated feature branch from the develop branch. This isolates your work so you can experiment and make changes without affecting other developers or the stable code.

特性分支是你大部分开发时间所在的地方。当你开始做一个新特性或修 bug 时，从 develop 分支创建一个专门的特性分支。这隔离了你的工作，让你可以实验和改动，而不影响其他开发者或稳定代码。

Giving these branches clear names tells other developers (and future you) what work is happening on that branch. Table 10-1 shows examples of good versus poor branch names.

给这些分支起清晰的名字，能告诉其他开发者（以及未来的你）这个分支上在做什么工作。表 10-1 展示了好分支名与差分支名的例子。

Good branch names好的分支名Poor branch names差的分支名
feature/user-authenticationfeature/user-authenticationmy-branchmy-branch
bugfix/login-timeoutbugfix/login-timeoutstuffstuff
enhancement/performance-optimizationenhancement/performance-optimizationfeature/123 (without context about what 123 refers to)feature/123（没有说明 123 指什么）
feature/JIRA-123-user-authentication (when using ticket tracking)feature/JIRA-123-user-authentication（使用工单跟踪时）
bugfix/GH-456-login-timeout (GitHub issue number)bugfix/GH-456-login-timeout（GitHub issue 编号）

Beyond feature branches, you may be wondering: “Why not just merge develop directly to main when you’re ready to release?” That is a really good question to ask. Release branches solve several issues that might come up when working in a team environment:

除了特性分支，你可能在想：“为什么不在准备发布时直接把 develop 合并到 main？”这个问题问得很好。发布分支解决了团队环境工作中可能出现的几个问题：

  • Stabilization period: While your release branch undergoes final testing and bug fixes, your team can continue adding new features to develop for the next release.稳定期：当你的发布分支在做最终测试和修 bug 时，团队可以继续向 develop 添加下个发布的新特性。
  • Release preparation: Version number updates, final documentation, and deployment configuration changes need a dedicated space that won’t interfere with ongoing development.发布准备：版本号更新、最终文档和部署配置改动需要一个专门的空间，不干扰正在进行的开发。
  • Quality gates: Many organizations require a “release candidate” phase where stakeholders can approve the exact code that will go to production.质量门禁：许多组织要求一个“发布候选”阶段，让干系人批准将要进入生产的确切代码。
  • Scheduled releases: If your team releases every two weeks, you need a way to “freeze” a set of features while continuing development for the next cycle.计划发布：如果团队每两周发布一次，你需要一种方式“冻结”一组特性，同时继续下一周期的开发。

Not every team needs release branches; it really depends on your organization’s practices. When your team has a formal release process or scheduled deployment windows, release branches provide good separation.

不是每个团队都需要发布分支；这确实取决于你们组织的实践。当团队有正式的发布流程或计划好的部署窗口时，发布分支能提供良好的分离。

You can also have hotfix branches. You also might be wondering: “Why do I need a separate branch for a hotfix when I can just use develop?” What happens when

你还可以有热修复分支。你可能还在想：“我直接用 develop 不就行了，为什么热修复还要单独开个分支？”当

原书第 261 页

production has a serious issue, but your develop branch contains half-finished features that aren’t ready for production?

生产出了严重问题，而你的 develop 分支里全是做了一半、还没准备好上生产的特性时，会发生什么？

Hotfix branches solve this emergency scenario by doing the following:

热修复分支通过以下方式解决这种紧急情况：

  • Bypassing unstable code: You can fix the production issue without deploying incomplete features from develop.绕开不稳定代码：你可以修复生产问题，而不必把 develop 上未完成的特性一起部署。
  • Maintaining clean history: The fix gets applied to both main (for immediate deployment) and develop (so it’s not lost in future releases).保持历史干净：修复同时应用到 main（用于立即部署）和 develop（以免在未来的发布中丢失）。
  • Speed and focus: Your team can work on the critical fix without worrying about other ongoing development work.速度与专注：团队可以专注于关键修复，而不必担心其他正在进行的开发工作。
  • Minimal risk: Since hotfixes branch from the stable main branch, you’re changing only what’s absolutely necessary.最小风险：由于热修复从稳定的 main 分支拉出，你只改绝对必要的部分。

In this section, you learned about the branch types in Git Flow. As you can see, each branch type serves a specific purpose in keeping your team’s work organized and properly versioned. The core branches (main and develop) provide stability and coordination, while the supporting branches (feature, release, and hotfix) handle specific tasks without disrupting the main workflow. This might seem overwhelming at first, but the more you work with a strategy like this one, the more you will see how it creates clear boundaries that help teams work together safely.

在本节中，你了解了 Git Flow 中的分支类型。如你所见，每种分支类型都有特定目的，让团队工作有序、版本得当。核心分支（main 和 develop）提供稳定性和协调，而辅助分支（feature、release、hotfix）处理特定任务而不打断主工作流。一开始这可能显得让人应接不暇，但你越使用这样的策略，就越能看到它如何创造清晰的边界，帮助团队安全协作。

The version control lifecycle

So, how do all of these branches work together to form a version control strategy? In Git Flow and many other strategies, development occurs in feature branches, gets merged into a develop branch, and finally placed into main after release, with hotfixes applied directly to both main and develop when necessary.

那么，所有这些分支如何协同形成一套版本控制策略？在 Git Flow 和许多其他策略中，开发在特性分支中进行，合并进 develop 分支，最后在发布后放入 main；必要时热修复直接应用到 main 和 develop 两者。

Git Flow 工作流如图 10-1 所示。

By understanding Git Flow, you have a solid foundation for team-based development, but remember that it’s just one approach among many. As you work with different teams and projects, you’ll encounter variations of these strategies, but the goals will remain the same. Provide a way to protect your code, isolate your work, and create a clear process for integrating changes. In the next section, we’ll explore how to automate deployments to ensure that your carefully managed code reaches production reliably and consistently.

理解了 Git Flow，你就为团队开发打下了坚实基础，但记住它只是众多方法之一。当你与不同团队和项目打交道时，会遇到这些策略的各种变体，但目标始终如一：提供一种保护代码、隔离工作、并为集成就更创建清晰流程的方式。下一节我们将探究如何自动化部署，确保你精心管理的代码可靠、一致地到达生产。

Deployment Automation

Manual deployments to production are often time-consuming, error-prone, and stressful. This is because you need to reproduce a deployment step-by-step with human intervention that involves code preparation and packaging, testing and verification, server preparation, deployment execution, post-deployment verification, and more. The good news is that we can address this problem by automating our deployments. In this section, you’ll learn about several key elements that will help streamline your deployment process.

手动部署到生产往往耗时、易错且压力大。这是因为你需要在人工干预下一步步重现部署，涉及代码准备与打包、测试与验证、服务器准备、部署执行、部署后验证等等。好消息是，我们可以通过自动化部署来解决这个问题。本节你将了解几个关键要素，它们能帮你精简部署流程。

原书第 263 页

Scripting deployments

Manual deployments are like handcrafting a custom bookshelf every single time you need one. Even if you’ve built the same bookshelf as before, you’re likely to miss a step, make small variations, or take much longer than necessary. Deployment automation is like having a factory that can build identical bookshelves to your exact specifications—precise, repeatable, and without human error. A deployment script serves as your factory instructions, documenting every step needed to consistently move your application from development to production.

手动部署就像每次需要一个书架时都手工打制一个定制书架。即使你以前打过同样的书架，也很可能漏一步、做出小差异、或花远超必要的时间。部署自动化就像拥有一座能按你的确切规格造出一模一样书架的工厂——精确、可重复、没有人为错误。部署脚本就是你的工厂作业指导书，记录把应用从开发一致地搬到生产所需的每一步。

Here’s a simple example of a deployment script that will run steps like creating directories, backing up existing directories, deploying the application, and starting it:

下面是一个简单的部署脚本示例，它会执行创建目录、备份现有目录、部署应用并启动它等步骤：

#!/bin/bash

# Configuration
APP_NAME="myapp"
JAR_FILE="target/${APP_NAME}.jar"
DEPLOY_DIR="/opt/applications/${APP_NAME}"
BACKUP_DIR="${DEPLOY_DIR}/backups"
LOG_FILE="${DEPLOY_DIR}/app.log"
PID_FILE="${DEPLOY_DIR}/${APP_NAME}.pid"
JVM_OPTS="-Xmx512m -Xms256m"

# Create directories
mkdir -p "${DEPLOY_DIR}" "${BACKUP_DIR}"

# Backup existing deployment
if [ -f "${DEPLOY_DIR}/${APP_NAME}.jar" ]; then
    mv "${DEPLOY_DIR}/${APP_NAME}.jar" \
    "${BACKUP_DIR}/${APP_NAME}-$(date +'%Y%m%d_%H%M%S').jar"
fi

# Stop running application
if [ -f "${PID_FILE}" ]; then
    kill $(cat "${PID_FILE}") 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "${PID_FILE}"
    sleep 2
fi

# Deploy new version
if [ -f "${JAR_FILE}" ]; then
    cp "${JAR_FILE}" "${DEPLOY_DIR}/${APP_NAME}.jar"
else
    echo "Error: JAR file not found: ${JAR_FILE}"
    exit 1
fi

# Start application
nohup java ${JVM_OPTS} -jar "${DEPLOY_DIR}/${APP_NAME}.jar" \
    > "${LOG_FILE}" 2>&1 &
原书第 264 页
echo $! > "${PID_FILE}"

# Quick health check
sleep 5
if kill -0 $(cat "${PID_FILE}") 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Deployment successful. PID: $(cat ${PID_FILE})"
else
    echo "Deployment failed. Check ${LOG_FILE} for details."
    exit 1
fi

While this example is basic, it illustrates key components of deployment automation:

虽然这个例子很基础，但它展示了部署自动化的关键组成部分：

  • Clear, documented steps清晰、文档化的步骤
  • Error handling错误处理
  • Backup procedures备份流程
  • Systematic approach系统化的方法

Even a simple script is better than no script. Start small and gradually improve your deployment automation over time. Your future self will thank you for putting in the time to automate this process now.

即使是简单的脚本也比没有脚本好。从小处着手，随时间逐步改进你的部署自动化。未来的你会感谢现在花时间把这个流程自动化的你。

Rollback procedures

We’ve established that automating your deployment will save time and reduce stress. However, even with a well-tested automated deployment, things can occasionally go wrong.

我们已经确立：自动化部署会节省时间、减轻压力。然而，即便有了经过充分测试的自动化部署，偶尔还是会出问题。

Nothing is perfect, so you need to be prepared for unexpected issues. Having a plan to quickly revert changes to a working state ensures that your customers can continue using your application without interruption.

没有什么是完美的，所以你需要为意外问题做好准备。有一个快速把改动回退到可用状态的计划，能确保你的客户不中断地继续使用应用。

Here’s an example of a rollback script that will look for the most recent backup, stop the application, restore, start, and then verify that the application is up and running correctly:

下面是一个回滚脚本示例：它会寻找最近的备份、停止应用、恢复、启动，然后验证应用是否正常运行：

#!/bin/bash

# Configuration (should match deploy.sh)
APP_NAME="myapp"
DEPLOY_DIR="/opt/applications/${APP_NAME}"
BACKUP_DIR="${DEPLOY_DIR}/backups"
LOG_FILE="${DEPLOY_DIR}/app.log"
PID_FILE="${DEPLOY_DIR}/${APP_NAME}.pid"
JVM_OPTS="-Xmx512m -Xms256m"

# Find most recent backup
LATEST_BACKUP=$(ls -t ${BACKUP_DIR}/${APP_NAME}-*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -1)
原书第 265 页
if [ -z "${LATEST_BACKUP}" ]; then
    echo "Error: No backup found in ${BACKUP_DIR}"
    exit 1
fi

# Stop current application
if [ -f "${PID_FILE}" ]; then
    kill $(cat "${PID_FILE}") 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "${PID_FILE}"
    sleep 2
fi

# Restore backup
cp "${LATEST_BACKUP}" "${DEPLOY_DIR}/${APP_NAME}.jar"

# Start application
nohup java ${JVM_OPTS} \
    -jar "${DEPLOY_DIR}/${APP_NAME}.jar" \
    > "${LOG_FILE}" 2>&1 &
echo $! >  "${PID_FILE}"

# Quick health check
sleep 5
if kill -0 $(cat "${PID_FILE}") 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Rollback successful. Restored: $(basename ${LATEST_BACKUP})"
    echo "Application running with PID: $(cat ${PID_FILE})"
else
    echo "Rollback failed. Check ${LOG_FILE} for details."
    exit 1
fi

Before implementing a rollback script, you should have these prerequisites in place:

在实现回滚脚本之前，你应当具备以下前提条件：

  • Verify that backup versions exist before deployment.部署前确认备份版本存在。
  • Test rollback procedures regularly.定期测试回滚流程。
  • Document database migration rollback steps.记录数据库迁移的回滚步骤。
  • Keep multiple backup versions.保留多个备份版本。
  • Monitor the system during rollback.回滚期间监控系统。

The goal of deployment automation isn’t just to save time. It’s to create a reliable, repeatable process that gives you confidence in your deployments. Start small, perhaps with a simple script that automates a few steps, and gradually build up to more comprehensive automation. Each improvement reduces risk and brings you closer to the ideal of predictable, stress-free deployments.

部署自动化的目标不只是节省时间。它是要创造一个可靠、可重复的流程，让你对部署有信心。从小处开始，也许先写一个自动化几个步骤的简单脚本，再逐步构建更全面的自动化。每一次改进都降低风险，让你更接近可预测、无压力部署的理想。

Deployment Strategies

There is no one-size-fits-all strategy when it comes to deploying your code into production. The strategy you choose for your application can be the difference between a smooth rollout and being on pager duty all weekend. Let’s take a look at some of the most popular approaches and when to choose them.

把代码部署到生产时，没有放之四海而皆准的策略。你为应用选择的策略，可能就是平滑发布与整个周末被叫呼之间的区别。让我们看看一些最流行的做法以及何时选择它们。

All-at-once deployment (big bang)

This strategy replaces the entire application in one go. The old version is completely swapped out for the new version at once. It’s simple to implement but carries a high risk, as any issues will immediately affect all users. There is no gradual transition period, making rollbacks complex if problems come up. This approach is best suited for smaller applications with thorough testing or in environments where downtime is acceptable.

这种策略一次性替换整个应用。旧版本立刻被新版本完全换掉。它实现简单，但风险很高，因为任何问题都会立刻影响所有用户。没有渐进过渡期，一旦出问题回滚会很复杂。这种做法最适合经过充分测试的较小应用，或允许停机的环境。

Big bang deployment is best for the following:

大爆炸式部署最适合以下情况：

  • Small applications with limited users用户有限的小型应用
  • Development and testing environments开发和测试环境
  • Systems that can tolerate some downtime能容忍一定停机的系统

Gradual deployment (phased approach)

A gradual deployment is like your favorite restaurant introducing a new recipe to a small number of customers at a time. This allows the chef to gather feedback, iterate, and gradually expand the recipe’s availability. Gradual deployment follows this approach by rolling out changes to a subset of users or servers before wider release. This controlled approach allows for early issue detection and course correction. Common examples include canary deployments (which deploy to a small percentage of users first) and rolling deployments (which gradually update servers one by one). Both can often be done with zero downtime using techniques like blue-green infrastructure or load balancer traffic shifting.

渐进式部署就像你最爱的餐厅一次只把新菜式介绍给少数顾客。这让厨师能收集反馈、迭代、逐步扩大菜式的供应范围。渐进式部署遵循这种方式：在更广泛发布之前，先把改动推给一小部分用户或服务器。这种受控方式能及早发现问题并纠正方向。常见例子包括金丝雀部署（先部署给一小部分用户）和滚动部署（逐台逐步更新服务器）。两者通常都可以用蓝绿基础设施或负载均衡器流量切换等技术实现零停机。

Gradual deployment is best for the following:

渐进式部署最适合以下情况：

  • Large-scale applications大规模应用
  • Features that benefit from user feedback能从用户反馈中获益的特性
  • Systems requiring careful monitoring需要仔细监控的系统

Zero downtime considerations

Whether you choose all-at-once or gradual deployment, you can minimize or eliminate downtime by using techniques like blue-green deployment (maintaining two

无论你选择一次性还是渐进式部署，都可以通过蓝绿部署（维护两套

identical environments and switching between them) or rolling updates. While more complex to set up, these provide the smoothest user experience for mission-critical applications and high-traffic services.

完全相同的环境并在它们之间切换）或滚动更新等技术，来最小化或消除停机。虽然搭建更复杂，但它们为关键任务应用和高流量服务提供最平滑的用户体验。

Choosing your strategy

When should you choose each approach? By now, you probably have already guessed that the answer is usually “it depends.” Consider factors like system complexity, tolerance for downtime, and monitoring capabilities when selecting the right strategy for your application.

你应该何时选择每种做法？到现在你大概已经猜到，答案通常是“看情况”。为应用选择正确策略时，要考虑系统复杂性、停机容忍度和监控能力等因素。
