Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment

In Chapter 5, you learned that automated testing provides confidence during the time of writing and committing code while helping identify issues early in the development lifecycle. But how can you ensure that these tests are run each time a release is promoted to a new environment like production? How do you guarantee that your code is built, tested, and deployed without the errors that manual human intervention can introduce?

在第 5 章你学到，自动化测试在写代码和提交代码时提供信心，同时帮你在开发生命周期早期发现问题。但你如何确保每次把发布提升到生产这样的新环境时都跑这些测试？你如何保证代码的构建、测试和部署没有人工干预可能引入的错误？

This is where continuous integration and continuous deployment, or CI/CD (or delivery) comes in. It’s a set of automated processes that takes your code from development all the way to production, where your users live. Continuous integration automatically combines and tests changes from your entire development team. Continuous delivery prepares your tested code for release, while continuous deployment can automatically release it to production.

这就是持续集成与持续部署，即 CI/CD（或持续交付）登场的地方。它是一组自动化流程，把你的代码从开发一路带到用户所在的生产。持续集成自动合并并测试整个开发团队的改动。持续交付把测好的代码准备好待发布，而持续部署可以自动把它发布到生产。

For example, say it’s your second week on the job and the team has asked you to help with the deployment of a smaller microservice. You open the lengthy deployment document that is filled with vague steps like “build the application,” “run the tests,” “update the database,” and “deploy to the server.” Your panic builds as you check off each item, knowing that if you miss even one little step, you could bring down production.

例如，假设你入职第二周，团队让你帮忙部署一个较小的微服务。你打开那份冗长的部署文档，里面全是含糊的步骤：“构建应用”“运行测试”“更新数据库”“部署到服务器”。你一边逐项打勾，恐慌一边累积，因为你知道哪怕漏掉一个小步骤，都可能搞垮生产。

Sounds pretty stressful, right? This is exactly why you need automation. Automation can eliminate a lot of issues by creating a repeatable, reliable process. The benefits of automation include the following:

听起来压力很大，对吧？这正是你需要自动化的原因。自动化通过创建可重复、可靠的流程来消除大量问题。自动化的好处包括：

  • Consistency: Remember the “works on my machine” scenario where the application works locally but has problems when promoted to another environment? When you automate your build process, you minimize that problem.一致性：还记得“在我机器上是好的”那种场景吗——应用本地能跑，提升到另一个环境就出问题？当你自动化构建流程时，就把这个问题降到最小。
原书第 268 页
  • Automated tests: Instead of relying on developers to run a suite of tests before committing their code, your CI/CD process can run tests automatically.自动化测试：CI/CD 流程可以自动运行测试，而不是依赖开发者在提交代码前手动跑测试套件。
  • Reduced stress: Instead of worrying about manually checking off each step in a deployment process, you can be sure your automation is run the same way every single time. A script never skips a step or mistypes a command.减轻压力：你不必再担心手动勾选部署流程中的每一步，可以确信自动化每次都以同样的方式运行。脚本绝不会跳过一步或敲错命令。
  • Early detection of integration issues: A well-defined CI/CD process can prevent issues from sneaking into production, saving you time and money.及早发现集成问题：定义良好的 CI/CD 流程能防止问题溜进生产，节省你的时间和金钱。
  • Reduced time between code and production: Go to production frequently by leveraging a well-defined automated process that minimizes deployment time. Remember, code has no real value until it reaches end users.缩短从代码到生产的时间：利用定义良好、把部署时间降到最小的自动化流程，频繁地上生产。记住，代码在到达终端用户之前没有真正的价值。

Building a basic CI/CD workflow

A CI/CD workflow is like a recipe: it defines the steps needed to take your code from development to production. Let’s look at a basic workflow:

CI/CD 工作流就像一份食谱：它定义了把代码从开发带到生产所需的步骤。我们来看一个基本工作流：

  • Code: A developer pushes code to the repository.代码：开发者把代码推送到仓库。
  • Build: The application is compiled and built.构建：应用被编译和构建。
  • Test: Automated tests are run.测试：运行自动化测试。
  • Package: The application is packaged for deployment.打包：应用被打包以备部署。
  • Deploy: The application is deployed to the target environment.部署：应用被部署到目标环境。

To put this into practice, let’s create a basic GitHub Actions workflow. A GitHub workflow is an automated process that you can set up in your GitHub repository to build, test, package, release, or deploy your code. GitHub Actions is a popular choice for implementing CI/CD pipelines because it’s easy to get started with and integrates naturally with your GitHub repository.

为了实践这一点，让我们创建一个基本的 GitHub Actions 工作流。GitHub 工作流是你可以在 GitHub 仓库中设置的自动化流程，用来构建、测试、打包、发布或部署代码。GitHub Actions 是实现 CI/CD 流水线的热门选择，因为它容易上手，且与你的 GitHub 仓库自然集成。

原书第 269 页

Here’s an example workflow file that implements these steps for a Java application:

下面是一个为 Java 应用实现这些步骤的工作流文件示例：

name: Java CI/CD Pipeline

on:
 push:
   branches: [ main ]
 pull_request:
   branches: [ main ]

jobs:
 build-and-test:
   runs-on: ubuntu-latest

   steps:
   # Check out your repository code
   - uses: actions/checkout@v4

   # Set up Java development environment
   - name: Set up JDK 25
     uses: actions/setup-java@v4
     with:
       java-version: '25'
       distribution: 'temurin'

   # Build the application
   - name: Build with Maven
     run: ./mvnw -B package --file pom.xml

   # Run automated tests
   - name: Run tests
     run: ./mvnw test

   # Package application (creates a JAR file)
   - name: Package application
     run: ./mvnw package -DskipTests

   # Store the package as an artifact
   - name: Upload artifact
     uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
     with:
       name: app-package
       path: target/*.jar

This workflow file demonstrates several key concepts:

这个工作流文件展示了几个关键概念：

  • The on section defines when the workflow runs (on push to main or PRs).on 部分定义工作流何时运行（推送到 main 或 PR 时）。
  • Each job runs in a fresh virtual environment (ubuntu-latest).每个 job 在全新的虚拟环境（ubuntu-latest）中运行。
  • Steps are executed sequentially, with each step depending on the success of previous steps.步骤按顺序执行，每一步都依赖前一步的成功。
原书第 270 页
  • The workflow handles building, testing, and packaging our application.该工作流处理我们应用的构建、测试和打包。

By implementing this workflow, you’ve automated several critical steps in your development process. When you push code or create a PR, GitHub automatically does the following:

通过实现这个工作流，你已经自动化了开发流程中的几个关键步骤。当你推送代码或创建 PR 时，GitHub 会自动做以下事情：

  • Builds your application to catch compilation errors early构建你的应用，及早捕获编译错误
  • Runs your test suite to catch potential bugs运行测试套件，捕获潜在 bug
  • Creates a deployable package创建可部署的包
  • Stores the package for later use存储该包以备后用

A CI/CD workflow automates the journey of code from development to production through a series of predefined steps. This automation eliminates manual intervention, catches errors early, enforces quality standards, and ultimately delivers software more reliably and effectively in a repeatable pattern.

CI/CD 工作流通过一系列预定义步骤，自动化代码从开发到生产的旅程。这种自动化消除了人工干预、及早捕获错误、强制执行质量标准，并最终以可重复的模式更可靠、更有效地交付软件。

Advanced CI/CD patterns

Don’t stress out about having to learn everything at once. Start simple and build on the foundations that you have learned in this chapter. Begin by automating your build and test process. As it begins to make more and more sense, you will feel more confident, and then you can gradually add more advanced deployment strategies.

别为了必须一次学完所有东西而焦虑。从简单开始，在本章学到的基础上构建。先自动化你的构建和测试流程。当它越来越说得通时，你会更有信心，然后再逐步加入更高级的部署策略。

As you move forward in your career, you’ll come across more sophisticated CI/CD patterns like these:

随着职业发展，你会遇到更复杂的 CI/CD 模式，比如：

  • Canary releases: Deploy new code to a small subset of users or servers first to test in production with minimal risk, expanding gradually if no issues are found.金丝雀发布：先把新代码部署给一小部分用户或服务器，以最小风险在生产中测试，如未发现问题则逐步扩大。
  • Blue-green deployments: Maintain two identical production environments (blue and green), with only one active at a time. New versions deploy to the inactive environment and, once verified, traffic switches over completely.蓝绿部署：维护两套相同的生产环境（蓝和绿），同一时间只有一套活跃。新版本部署到不活跃的那套，验证后流量完全切换过去。

Here are some ways to introduce advanced patterns and gradually improve your CI/CD process:

以下是一些引入高级模式、逐步改进 CI/CD 流程的方式：

  1. Start with a basic pipeline that builds and tests your code.从一个构建和测试代码的基本流水线开始。
  2. Gradually incorporate more automated checks and validations.逐步加入更多自动化检查和验证。
  3. Maintain a fast pipeline to ensure quick feedback loops.保持快速的流水线，确保快速的反馈回路。
  4. Regularly monitor and optimize your pipeline based on team needs.根据团队需求定期监控和优化流水线。
  5. Document your pipeline to facilitate team collaboration.为流水线编写文档，以便团队协作。

CI/CD is not just about tools and automation. It is about fostering a culture of continuous improvement and reliable software delivery. By embracing these practices early in your career, you’ll build a strong foundation for professional growth and become an invaluable team member.

CI/CD 不只是关于工具和自动化。它关乎培育一种持续改进和可靠软件交付的文化。在职业生涯早期就拥抱这些实践，你会为职业成长打下坚实基础，成为团队中不可或缺的一员。

Production System Monitoring and Maintenance

You have written your code, tested it thoroughly, and now it’s ready for production. Your application went through the proper CI/CD pipeline and is now live in production. It’s time to kick up your feet and relax, right? Not quite. The journey of a working application on your machine to a reliable system in production is an ongoing one.

你写好了代码，充分测试过，现在它准备好上生产了。你的应用经过了正规的 CI/CD 流水线，现在已经在生产上线。是时候翘起脚放松了，对吧？还差得远。从你机器上一个能跑的应用，到生产中一个可靠的系统，这段旅程是持续不断的。

Monitoring

Proper monitoring and logging can tell you a lot about the state of your application. Without these in place, you won’t know how your system is performing currently or over time. Too many developers want to throw their app into production and hope for the best. They think that no news is good news. The truth is, users rarely tell you when something is wrong. They just leave.

恰当的监控和日志能告诉你关于应用状态的很多信息。没有它们，你不会知道系统当前或随时间表现如何。太多开发者想把应用扔到生产里然后祈祷一切顺利。他们以为没消息就是好消息。真相是，用户很少在出问题时告诉你。他们只是离开。

Your application relies on two types of monitoring systems:

你的应用依赖两类监控系统：

  • Real-time monitoring: Tracks what’s happening right now. Is your application’s response time too slow? Is the server load or throughput too high? Individual metrics never tell the complete story. A 300 ms response time might seem fast, but if your application normally responds in 50 ms, this could indicate a problem.实时监控：追踪此刻正在发生什么。应用响应时间是不是太慢？服务器负载或吞吐量是不是太高？单个指标永远讲不出完整故事。300 毫秒的响应时间看起来很快，但如果你的应用通常 50 毫秒就响应，这可能预示着问题。
  • Logs: Serve as your historical record. When issues arise, good logs help you reconstruct what went wrong and when. They provide the context for troubleshooting.日志：充当你的历史记录。问题出现时，好日志帮你重建出了什么问题、何时出的。它们为排查故障提供上下文。

After experiencing several critical incidents with our application, we established these vital monitoring rules:

在我们的应用经历了几次重大事故之后，我们定下了这些至关重要的监控规则：

  1. Log information you will need when problems occur.记录问题发生时你会需要的信息。
  2. Always include timestamps and user identifiers.始终包含时间戳和用户标识符。
  3. Mark errors as errors. Do not bury important alerts in info logs.把错误标记为错误。别把重要警报埋在 info 日志里。
  4. Keep private data out of logs (no passwords or personal details).把隐私数据挡在日志之外（不要记录密码或个人细节）。
  5. Delete old logs before they consume your storage.在旧日志吃光你的存储之前删除它们。

从简单开始

Keep your monitoring system simple at first. Watch your response times, error counts, and server resources. That’s enough to start. The fancy tools can come later.
一开始让你的监控系统保持简单。盯着响应时间、错误数和服务器资源就够了。花哨的工具以后再说。

Good monitoring provides peace of mind. Problems will eventually occur; that is the nature of software. When they do, you’ll be thankful you have metrics and logs to help you diagnose and fix issues quickly.

一旦有了日志和指标，AI 工具可以显著增强你的监控能力。AI 可以在海量日志中搜索，识别可能预示新问题正在酝酿的异常或模式，赶在它们变得严重之前。此外，AI 可以根据你的指标数据帮你生成监控仪表盘——这传统上需要繁琐的手动配置——给你一个坚实的起点，加速仪表盘创建过程。

System Maintenance

When a system is deployed to production, it is not the end of the journey; it’s just the beginning. System maintenance is a critical aspect of keeping software running efficiently, securely, and reliably. This section covers how to maintain the production system to prevent costly issues and ensure optimal performance.

当一个系统部署到生产，它不是旅程的终点；而只是起点。系统维护是让软件高效、安全、可靠运行的关键环节。本节介绍如何维护生产系统，以预防代价高昂的问题并确保最佳性能。

Keeping systems up-to-date

Software that has been deployed to production needs regular maintenance. While everything is performing well in production, it might be tempting to postpone maintenance, but this would be a mistake. What might start off as minor, inexpensive issues can quickly transform into major, costly problems.

已部署到生产的软件需要定期维护。虽然生产中一切表现良好，你可能很想推迟维护，但这会是个错误。一开始可能是小而廉价的问题，会迅速变成大而昂贵的问题。

When you are dealing with systems that users depend on, the costs are high. Critical infrastructure requires consistent upkeep to ensure safety and reliability. But somehow in software development, teams will frequently delay necessary updates despite the risks.

当你面对用户依赖的系统时，代价是高昂的。关键基础设施需要持续维护来确保安全和可靠。但不知怎的，在软件开发中，团队常常不顾风险而推迟必要的更新。

System updates

Operating system updates and security patches form your first line of defense for running into major, costly problems. These updates often address the following:

操作系统更新和安全补丁是你避免撞上重大、昂贵问题的第一道防线。这些更新通常解决以下问题：

  • Critical security vulnerabilities关键安全漏洞
  • Performance improvements性能改进
  • Bug fixes缺陷修复
  • New features and capabilities新特性和新能力

Never ignore security updates. While feature updates can sometimes wait, security patches should be applied promptly to protect your systems from vulnerabilities.

永远不要忽视安全更新。虽然特性更新有时可以等，但安全补丁应当及时应用，以保护你的系统免受漏洞攻击。

Dependency management

Dependency management is arguably the most overlooked aspect of system maintenance. Your application may rely on dozens or even hundreds of external libraries, each potentially harboring security vulnerabilities. Remember the SBOMs we discussed earlier in this chapter? This is exactly why maintaining an accurate SBOM is important for tracking and updating your dependencies.

依赖管理可以说是系统维护中最被忽视的一环。你的应用可能依赖几十甚至几百个外部库，每个都可能暗藏安全漏洞。还记得本章前面讨论的 SBOM 吗？这正是为什么维护一份准确的 SBOM 对追踪和更新依赖很重要。

The following code shows a dependency in a Java app that declares an outdated version with known vulnerabilities:

下面的代码展示了一个 Java 应用中的依赖，它声明了一个有已知漏洞的过时版本：

// Example dependency in pom.xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
    <version>2.5.5</version>  // Outdated version with known vulnerabilities
</dependency>

When you generate an SBOM for this application, security tools can scan it against vulnerability databases to identify that version 2.5.5 has known security issues and recommend updating to a newer, secure version.

当你为这个应用生成 SBOM 时，安全工具可以把它与漏洞数据库比对扫描，识别出 2.5.5 版本有已知安全问题，并建议更新到更新、更安全的版本。

Modern build tools like Maven and Gradle offer dependency analyzers that can alert you to known vulnerabilities. To catch these issues early, set up automated scans. In this example, a GitHub Action runs dependency checks on your code:

Maven 和 Gradle 等现代构建工具提供依赖分析器，能就已知漏洞向你发出警报。为了及早发现这些问题，设置自动化扫描。在这个例子中，一个 GitHub Action 对你的代码运行依赖检查：

// Example GitHub Actions workflow snippet
jobs:
  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Run Dependency Check
        uses: dependency-check/Dependency-Check@main

Taking action

You can start to improve system maintenance by establishing an update policy for your team or project:

你可以通过为团队或项目建立更新策略来着手改进系统维护：

  1. Set regular update intervals.设定固定的更新间隔。
  2. Define emergency patch procedures.定义紧急补丁流程。
  3. Implement automated scanning.实施自动化扫描。
  4. Document update processes.记录更新流程。
  5. Maintain an update log.维护更新日志。

Remember, prevention costs less than recovery. Make system updates a priority in your development workflow. Set calendar reminders for regular update reviews. Despite automation, human oversight remains crucial for maintaining system health.

记住，预防比恢复便宜。把系统更新作为开发工作流中的优先事项。为定期更新评审设置日历提醒。尽管有自动化，人工监督对于维持系统健康仍然至关重要。

Wrapping Up

Moving your code from the safety of your local machine to the unpredictable world of production can be intimidating at first. Just know that you are not alone and most developers have felt that same stress at one point in their career. Preparation is the key to ensuring you have a good deployment process in place. Taking code to production is a skill that will improve over time with experience.

把代码从本地机器的安全地带搬到生产这个不可预测的世界，一开始可能令人生畏。只要知道你并不孤单，大多数开发者在职业生涯中都体会过同样的压力。准备是确保你有一套良好部署流程的关键。把代码送上生产是一项会随经验增长而精进的技能。

Remember these key takeaways:

记住这些要点：

  • Think production ready from day one. Consider performance, security, and error handling while you code.从第一天起就想着可上线。写代码时就考虑性能、安全和错误处理。
  • Configure your applications properly for different environments by using environment variables and feature flags.使用环境变量和特性开关，为不同环境恰当配置应用。
  • Monitor your application’s health and set up proper logging, but never log sensitive data.监控应用健康状况并建立恰当的日志，但绝不记录敏感数据。
  • Use version control strategies like Git Flow to collaborate safely with your team.使用 Git Flow 之类的版本控制策略与团队安全协作。
  • Automate your deployments with CI/CD to make them reliable and repeatable.用 CI/CD 自动化部署，让它们可靠、可重复。
  • Remember, your users don’t care if the application works on your machine. They care if it works on theirs.记住，你的用户不在乎应用在你机器上能不能跑。他们在乎在自己机器上能不能跑。

As you begin deploying your own applications to production, you will face challenges and sometimes might even fail: that is OK. Each failure you encounter is a chance to learn something new and will make you a better software engineer.

当你开始把自己的应用部署到生产时，你会面对挑战，有时甚至会失败：这没关系。你遇到的每一次失败都是学习新东西的机会，会让你成为更好的软件工程师。

原书第 275 页

Focus on building good habits now, and production deployments will become a natural part of your development workflow. Before long, you will be an experienced developer helping others ship code to the promised land of production.

现在就专注养成好习惯，生产部署会自然成为你开发工作流的一部分。用不了多久，你就会成为一个资深开发者，帮助别人把代码送上生产的应许之地。

Putting It into Practice

It’s hard to envision how an entire application will perform in production, so incrementally adopt some of the best practices you learned in this chapter. The following are good habits that can be applied at various points before deploying to production. The next time you’re assigned a feature, pick one or two items from each of these categories to apply to your work. Don’t try to do everything at once; instead, focus on building these habits gradually.

很难预想整个应用在生产中会如何表现，所以增量式地采用你在本章学到的一些最佳实践。以下是一些好习惯，可以在部署到生产前的各个节点应用。下次你被分配一个特性时，从每个类别中挑一两样应用到你的工作中。别想一次全做；相反，专注逐步养成这些习惯。

Before you code:

写代码之前：

  • Create a simple list of what could go wrong with your feature.列一个简单清单，写下你的特性可能出什么问题。
  • Plan what information you might need to log to debug these issues.计划一下需要记录哪些信息来调试这些问题。
  • Identify what configuration might change from your local machine to other environments in your workflow.识别从你本机到工作流中其他环境时，哪些配置可能变化。

While coding:

写代码时：

  • Create a feature branch with a clear, descriptive name before starting work.开始工作前，创建一个名字清晰、有描述性的特性分支。
  • Add basic error handling for the top three things that could fail.为最可能失败的三件事加上基本的错误处理。
  • Include logging statements for key actions (but avoid logging sensitive data!).为关键操作加上日志语句（但避免记录敏感数据！）。
  • Write a test that mimics real user behavior.写一个模拟真实用户行为的测试。
  • Use configuration values for anything that might change between environments.对任何可能在环境间变化的东西使用配置值。

Before deployment:

部署之前：

  • Write down your deployment steps as you do them.边做边写下你的部署步骤。
  • Create a simple rollback plan. How would you turn off this feature if things go wrong?制定一个简单的回滚计划。如果出问题，你会怎么关掉这个特性？
  • Have a teammate review your changes with production in mind.让一个同事带着生产环境的眼光评审你的改动。

After deployment:

部署之后：

  • Begin monitoring your logs after deployment for an hour or two. Does anything stand out?部署后花一两个小时监控日志。有没有什么扎眼的？
原书第 276 页
  • Put together a retrospective about this deployment. This is a meeting or discussion held after completing a project or deployment, where the team can reflect on what went well, what challenges they faced, and what lessons can be learned.为这次部署做一次回顾。回顾会是在完成项目或部署后召开的会议或讨论，团队可以反思哪些做得好、遇到了哪些挑战、能学到什么教训。
